benefits: Hides implementation details: casual readers can no longer skim your logic at a glance.
Shrinks casual copying: renamed identifiers and escaped strings raise the effort bar for copy-paste reuse.
Strips comments automatically: internal notes and TODOs never ship to the browser.
Keeps code working: transformations preserve semantics, so the output runs exactly like the input.

faqs.a: It rewrites readable JavaScript into a harder-to-read but functionally identical form: identifiers become short generated names, string contents become hex escapes, and comments and extra whitespace are removed.
faqs.q: What does a JavaScript obfuscator do?

faqs.a: No. Obfuscation is a speed bump, not a lock. Anyone determined can reformat and trace the code with browser developer tools. Never put secrets, passwords, or API keys in client-side code - obfuscated or not.
faqs.q: Does obfuscation make my code secure?

faqs.a: Yes. Renaming only touches declared local identifiers, strings keep their exact values through hex escapes, and whitespace collapsing never crosses line boundaries, so the output behaves identically. Still, always test the obfuscated file before deploying it.
faqs.q: Will the obfuscated code still work?

faqs.a: Yes - they are never renamed. The tool keeps a built-in list of language keywords and common browser and Node globals (window, document, console, Math, JSON, and others) untouched.
faqs.q: Are built-ins like console and Math renamed?

faqs.a: It handles all of them: single quotes, double quotes, and template literals. Inside template literals, ${...} interpolations are preserved while the surrounding text is escaped.
Obfuscation only slows readers down. Minification also shrinks file size for faster loading. This tool does light whitespace collapsing; pair it with a real minifier for production size savings.

javascript-obfuscator.formula:
rename:  declared name  ->  _0x0, _0x1, _0x2, ... (base-36 counter)
escape:  "Hi"  ->  "\x48\x69"   (every char becomes a hex escape)
strip:   // comment  ->  removed,   /* block */  ->  single space
Order: scan strings/comments -> mask strings -> rename identifiers -> collapse spaces -> restore escaped strings.

keyFacts: Obfuscation rewrites code to be hard to read while keeping it functionally identical - it is not encryption.
This tool applies three transforms: identifier renaming (_0x0, _0x1, ...), string hex-escaping (\xNN), and comment/whitespace removal.
Renaming only affects identifiers declared with var, let, const, function, or class. Function parameters are left as-is.
Language keywords and common globals (window, document, console, Math, JSON, ...) are never renamed.
Template literal ${...} interpolations are preserved; only the surrounding text is escaped.
Comment stripping is string-aware: // inside a URL string is not treated as a comment.

Function parameters and object properties are not renamed, only declared variable, function, and class names.
Code using import/export needs manual review: renaming can break module bindings.
Very large files (megabytes) may take a moment to process since everything runs on the main thread.
